r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding: Every claim reproduced independently; nothing accepted on the report. (1) Crash pre/post with real exit codes: pre-fix EXIT 1 / never answered, post-fix EXIT 0 / isError answer. (2) Guard width is OSError, not bare Exception, at :213 and :218 -- read in source, and correct: json.dumps at :209 sits OUTSIDE both guards, so a programming error still propagates rather than hiding behind a telemetry message. (3) Loss reported on stderr: both drops named on stderr with the lost record, observed in the probe. (5) stdout stays pure JSON-RPC while telemetry fails -- and that check is NOT a check that cannot fail: mutating _report_dropped_telemetry to write to stdout turns test_stdout_stays_pure_json_rpc_when_telemetry_fails red. (6) The test is genuinely red pre-fix: isolated tree from git archive a69bbac4 (helper absent, _log unguarded at :181/:184 confirmed; checklist_engine.py byte-identical to HEAD so the engine is not a variable) -> 5 failed, 2 passed. I did NOT use the handoff's in-place git checkout recipe: lanes B and C run concurrently in this worktree and briefly reverting a shared file could corrupt them; the isolated tree is strictly more faithful. (7) SPINE_CALLLOG / SPINE_START_MARKER / SPINE_REJECTION_LOG overrides still work -- the three module-level os.environ.get lines (:162, :167, :177) are outside the diff hunk, and all three are exercised green by test_mcp_lifecycle.py:102-103, test_mcp_friction_capture.py:99 and test_mcp_door_telemetry.py:118-120. THE HANDOFF'S QUESTION -- are both pre-fix passes benign? Yes, and the implementer's disclosure is complete. test_stdout_stays_pure... passes pre-fix because a dead door's stdout holds only the initialize reply, which is valid JSON-RPC; disclosed, and shown above to have a reachable failing state. The second, test_healthy_run_writes_both_telemetry_files, is the declared positive control -- it is SUPPOSED to pass on both trees, since that is exactly how it stops a fix that simply stopped writing telemetry, and it is documented as such in its own docstring and the module docstring. I proved it can fail: mutating _log to an immediate return (the 'stopped writing telemetry' fix) turns it red (4 failed, 3 passed). Correction to my first pass at this item: I had cited the collapsed-guard mutant for that, which is wrong -- the control survives that one. The no-write mutant is the one that kills it. Evidence artifacts exist and are fresh from this run: evidence/pre-fix-probes.txt (05:44), post-fix-probes.txt (05:59), red-test.txt (06:04).

r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: CRITERION 4 -- MY OWN COUNT: FOUR filesystem writes in the module, confirming the two prior passes. Enumerated mechanically, not by eye: an ast.walk over scripts/mcp_spine_server.py for every write-capable call site returns 12, which classify as 4 filesystem writes and 8 non-filesystem. The four: (a) :211-212 CALLLOG append, telemetry, guarded except OSError :213; (b) :217 START_MARKER.write_text, telemetry, guarded except OSError :218; (c) :527-528 REJECTIONLOG append in _log_rejection, telemetry, guarded except OSError :529 (pre-existing, issue #541); (d) :570 path.write_text in _write_amend_delta. The eight non-filesystem: :187 and :530 sys.stderr, :1402 and :1410 sys.stdout (the JSON-RPC channel), :485 and :493 err.write into an io.StringIO buffer (:479, in-memory, cannot raise OSError), and :212/:528 which are the fh.write halves of (a) and (c). So NO telemetry write anywhere in the module remains unguarded -- three of three. The fourth, (d), is deliberately NOT telemetry and correctly not best-effort: it materialises the delta the engine must then read, so it must fail the call. It is unguarded at the write site but its sole call site (:1324-1330, verified sole by grep) catches OSError and returns _tool_error('spine_amend: could not write delta file: ...'). I did not take that on reading: probing spine_amend against the missing directory returns isError:true with that exact message at EXIT 0, and probing an unknown tool -- the only path that reaches _log_rejection -- returns isError:true at EXIT 0 with 'REJECTION CAPTURE FAILED' on stderr. All four write paths are non-fatal, and the implementer's own tests exercise only (a) and (b), so (c) and (d) rest on my probes. HANDOFF CONSTRAINTS all honoured: __pycache__ cleared before every measurement (worktree and both temp trees); every validation ran against a subprocess I launched, never this session's own door; the suite ran with env -u SPINE_FILE -u SPINE_SESSION -u SPINE_PARENT -> 96 passed, 10 subtests passed. OBSERVATION, not a blocker, out of gate scope: docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md 'Writing Files On Windows' requires encoding='utf-8', newline='\n' on EVERY write. _log_rejection at :527 passes newline='\n'; the two _log writes at :211 and :217 pass encoding only, so on Windows mcp_calls.jsonl and mcp_server_started get CRLF while mcp_rejections.jsonl gets LF. This is PRE-EXISTING -- the diff wrapped those two calls in guards without altering their arguments, and introduced no new file write -- so it is not a regression and does not bar g1. Flagged as a triage candidate.

r6-fowler.title: Refactoring pass (Fowler code smells)
r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards — an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to .agent-work/cleanup-a-door/FOWLER_PASS.json (from templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json), run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py .agent-work/cleanup-a-door/FOWLER_PASS.json (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. This item's postcondition command resolves the record path from cleanup-a-door alone -- the same substitution you already make everywhere else in this survey (line 2) -- so no separate placeholder to fill and no way to leave it stale. REPAIR PATH -- only if the record path ever needs to move off that fixed convention, correct it through the engine with `amend --delta <file>` whose single op is `retext-check` on this item's c1, never by hand-editing this survey. There, --authority is the dispatching Commander named in your reviewer handoff (never a string you invent), and --reason is why the path changed. Do NOT silently skip this item.

r6-fowler.finding: Refactoring pass run over commit 0060dc08; record at .agent-work/cleanup-a-door/FOWLER_PASS.json, rail scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py exits 0 (smells=12, flagged=['duplicated-code'], overridden=['comments-as-deodorant']). All 12 baseline smells visited. ONE FLAGGED -- duplicated-code: _report_dropped_telemetry's body (:187-191) and the inline stderr block inside _log_rejection (:530-534) are the same five lines apart from one label ('TELEMETRY WRITE FAILED' vs 'REJECTION CAPTURE FAILED'). The implementer described the helper as reusing _log_rejection's shape, and it reused that shape by copying rather than extracting; one _report_lost_record(kind, target, exc, lost) would carry both and keep the two lost-record diagnostics guaranteed to match each other. The reason the standard subordinates the smell is that the prose is rationale, not restatement: why OSError and not bare Exception, why two separate guards, why stderr and never stdout, and the #604 history. None of that is recoverable from the code, which is the line between deodorant and rationale. The other ten are absent, each with the reasoning recorded rather than left blank -- notably speculative-generality, where the helper's two real call sites make the seam real rather than hypothetical, and primitive-obsession, where lost being a str is deliberate so the reported record is byte-identical to the one that would have been written.

consolidation.summary: APPROVE. Issue #604 is fixed and the fix is proven, every claim reproduced independently rather than accepted. Crash pre/post by real subprocess exit code: at a69bbac4 the door dies on its own call log (EXIT 1, never answered); at HEAD the same probe is EXIT 0 with a truthful {isError: true, FileNotFoundError}. The guard is OSError and not bare Exception (:213, :218), and json.dumps at :209 sits outside it so programming errors still propagate. Both drops are reported on stderr with the lost record. My own mechanical enumeration -- an ast.walk, not a read-by-eye -- finds FOUR filesystem writes in the module, confirming the two prior passes: three are telemetry (:211, :217, :527) and all three are guarded; the fourth (:570, _write_amend_delta) is functional rather than telemetry and correctly fails the CALL, not the process, which I proved by probe rather than by reading. The regression test genuinely discriminates: 5 failed / 2 passed on an isolated pre-fix tree, 96 passed / 10 subtests on HEAD. I also killed the two remaining could-not-fail worries by mutation -- rerouting the drop report to stdout turns the stdout-purity test red, and reducing _log to an immediate return turns the positive control red -- so the handoff's question is answered: both pre-fix passes are benign and the implementer's disclosure was complete. The separate-guards choice is pinned, not decorative: collapsing them into one try turns exactly 2 of the 7 tests red. Three non-blocking triage candidates (tc1 CRLF newline discipline on _log's two writes, pre-existing; tc2 map/ids.jsonl is 0 bytes so no map anchor resolves, confirming the handoff's own tc1; tc3 the drop-report duplication between :187-191 and :530-534). NOT CHECKED, stated as scoped nulls: fail-closed refusal wording for a missing or unbound spine (gate g3's, and the raw FileNotFoundError is the correct g1 outcome); anything under the fenced files; Windows behaviour, since every measurement here was on Linux 3.12.3; and whether this local green matches CI's pin.
